_comment: [FABLE-5] sq-hmd7l.15 — PINNED published W3C JSON-LD 1.1 conformance results for the
jsonld-bench peers (bench/competitors.json: jsonld-js, titanium-json-ld), plus sparq's
own MEASURED lane counts. Every peer number is FETCHED from the cited source on the
retrieval date — never estimated. Rendered as a table (with the comparability caveats)
COMPARABILITY CAVEATS (load-bearing — do not collapse into one pass-rate column):
1. DENOMINATORS DIFFER BY SUITE SNAPSHOT. The W3C EARL report and Titanium's README
were generated against older w3c/json-ld-api revisions (e.g. expand total 376)
than sparq's pinned revision (expand total 385; pin in scripts/fetch-jsonld-tests.sh).
Percentages are only comparable within a row's own denominator.
2. ORACLES DIFFER FOR sparq's compact + frame LANES. sparq's compact/frame counts use a
round-trip RDF losslessness oracle (reparse(compact(D,ctx)) == D), NOT the suite's
structural expected-document assertion the peers report against — so those two rows
are NOT 1:1 comparable and are marked oracle=roundtrip-rdf. sparq's expand/flatten
(document-level deep-equality) and toRdf/fromRdf (dataset equality) lanes ARE the
same assertion shape the peers run.
3. SKIP TAXONOMY. sparq SKIPS (never counts) NegativeEvaluationTests in the expand lane
and the option-feature/remote buckets; peers typically run negatives. pass/fail/skip
triples are given so no skip is silently folded into a pass rate.

sparq.source: MEASURED in-tree: cargo test -p sparq-conformance --features jsonld-suite --test jsonld_suite

compact.oracle: roundtrip-rdf (NOT the suite's structural assertion — see caveat 2)

frame.oracle: roundtrip-rdf-shaped (NOT the suite's structural assertion — see caveat 2)

jsonld-js.note: percentage-passed rows as published; totals are the REPORT's manifest sizes (older suite snapshot than sparq's pin — caveat 1)

titanium-json-ld.source: titanium-json-ld README conformance table, https://github.com/filip26/titanium-json-ld (commit ab0ccd4b50bdbd5d25422c486233f59e5ad8a679, 2026-06-06); EARL cross-reference https://w3c.github.io/json-ld-api/reports/#subj_Titanium_JSON_LD_Java
titanium-json-ld.note: self-published table (newer than the EARL snapshot, which lists 98.1% expansion / 98.0% compaction / 96.7% framing / 97.6% toRdf for Titanium)
